# ar-1 -- the site access point (#30).
#
# interface is the real radio, moved into this container's own network
# namespace by the "interfaces" list in this recipe. It is named by
# its mac device mapping, radio-ap (cix ADR-0345, 1.2.0): inside it is
# radio-ap whatever the kernel called it on the host, so neither this
# file nor the recipe names a probe-order name like wlan0 any more. A
# host running this needs that mapping first, on the radio's permanent
# address:
#   cixctl devicemap create --name=radio-ap --kind=mac --selector=MAC
# and without it the create is refused with a 400 naming radio-ap.
# It is a netdev
# passthrough, not a USB device passthrough: a wireless adapter is
# claimed by its driver on the host, and what a container needs is the
# resulting interface, not the USB endpoint (daemon/src/device.c says
# so in as many words).
#
# bridge is the whole reason ADR-0264 exists. hostapd puts the radio into
# br0 and will create br0 if it is missing -- but it knows nothing
# about this container's other interfaces and would never enslave one,
# so a bridge hostapd built alone would carry the radio and nothing
# else. Cix builds br0 first, with the access-network veth already in
# it, and hostapd then adds the radio to the bridge it finds. Wireless
# clients and the wired access segment are one layer-2 domain.
#
# ctrl_interface is what the hostapd_cli console attaches to.
#
interface=radio-ap
bridge=br0
driver=nl80211
ctrl_interface=/run/hostapd

#
# hostapd logs "rfkill: Cannot open RFKILL control device" here, every
# start, and it is harmless TODAY rather than harmless. There is no
# /dev/rfkill in this container, so hostapd cannot read or clear a
# soft block. Nothing sets one at present and the AP comes up fine --
# but if a radio ever is soft-blocked, hostapd inside here has no way
# to see why it cannot transmit, and the message above is the only
# clue it will give. Passing /dev/rfkill through is the fix if that
# ever happens; it is not done now because a device passthrough that
# nothing needs is a permission granted for no reason.
#

#
# NO COUNTRY CODE HERE, AND THERE NEVER CAN BE ONE.
#
# The country is the HOST's, set by cixd from `cixctl wireless set`
# (cix ADR-0354, #355), and this host's is GB. The kernel holds one
# regulatory domain for the whole host and accepts it only from
# CAP_NET_ADMIN in the initial user namespace (NL80211_CMD_REQ_SET_REG
# is GENL_ADMIN_PERM, kernel 7.2.12). This container is in a user
# namespace, so a country_code here is refused, every start, with
#   wlan0: interface state UNINITIALIZED->COUNTRY_UPDATE
#   Failed to set country code
# which is what 1.0.8 and 1.1.0 did. hostapd sends the request whenever
# a country is set, even one the kernel already has, so the line has to
# be absent rather than merely correct. ieee80211d needs a country, so
# it is absent too.
#
# The regulatory database does load: kernel 7.2.3-8 onwards builds
# regulatory.db in with CONFIG_EXTRA_FIRMWARE, and on 2026-10-24 the
# host moved from the world domain 00 to GB as soon as cixd asked.
#
#
# Band and channel: 5 GHz, channel 36 (the owner's choice, 2026-10-24).
#
# Under the world domain every 5 GHz channel was NO-IR, so an AP could
# not start there and this ran 2.4 GHz channel 6. Under GB, measured on
# this radio the same day, channels 36-48 carry 23 dBm with no NO-IR,
# and 52-64 and 100-144 need radar detection. 36 is the bottom of
# UNII-1 and needs none, so the AP beacons at once instead of waiting
# out a DFS scan, and ieee80211h is not needed.
#
# NO VHT (802.11ac) HERE, AND THAT IS A BUILD FACT RATHER THAN A CHOICE.
#
# hostapd rejected ieee80211ac, vht_oper_chwidth and
# vht_oper_centr_freq_seg0_idx as "unknown configuration item" and
# refused to start -- upstream's defconfig, which hostapd.recipe uses
# as-is, leaves CONFIG_IEEE80211AC commented out, so the binary has no
# VHT support compiled in. An unknown item is fatal to hostapd, not a
# warning, so these cannot simply be left in place hopefully. The AP
# therefore runs 802.11n (HT) on 5 GHz.
#
hw_mode=a
channel=36
ieee80211n=1

#
# The network itself.
#
# WPA2-PSK with CCMP only. TKIP is not offered at all -- it is broken,
# and offering it as a fallback is how a network ends up negotiating it.
#
# The passphrase below is a secret placeholder in the committed
# recipe, substituted from the apply request rather than stored here.
# This file is in git; the passphrase is not, and never will be.
#
# The placeholder is deliberately not spelled out in this comment:
# cixd warns when a RENDERED container still contains the token prefix,
# and prose describing it trips that check exactly as a forgotten
# secret would. A warning that cries wolf at documentation is worse
# than no warning.
#
ssid=cix
wpa=2
wpa_key_mgmt=WPA-PSK
rsn_pairwise=CCMP
wpa_passphrase={{SECRET:WIFI_PASSPHRASE}}

# Clients talk to each other through the bridge, which is what a normal
# wireless LAN does. Set to 1 to isolate them from one another.
ap_isolate=0

# hostapd_cli needs a /tmp, and this image has none.
#
# hostapd_cli connects to hostapd by creating its OWN client socket
# first, and wpa_ctrl.c hardcodes that to /tmp. This platform's
# minimal images have /run and no /tmp at all (measured: GET
# .../files?path=/tmp returns 404 while /run and /run/hostapd are
# both directories), so the console attached, printed "Could not
# connect to hostapd" and could tell nobody why.
#
# Declaring a file is how a container asks for a directory here,
# which is a blunt way to say it. The general fix is for every
# container to have a /tmp the way ADR-0119 gave every container a
# /run -- this is the third time its absence has cost real
# debugging (iptables, gcc, now this) and it is filed rather than
# solved inside one AP's recipe.
